title: Frontend entry domain dom event flow
topic: Frontend entry domain dom event flow
question: When you click on a nested element, how does the browser decide which event handlers run, and in what order?
idealAnswer:
The DOM is a tree, and a click dispatches an event that travels through three phases: capturing (root down to target), target, and bubbling (target back up to root)

By default, addEventListener attaches handlers to the bubbling phase, so a handler on a parent fires after the handler on the clicked child

Passing { capture: true } attaches the handler to the capturing phase instead, so it runs on the way down, before the target's own handler

event.stopPropagation() stops the event from continuing to bubble (or capture) further, while event.preventDefault() stops the browser's default action but does not stop propagation, these are separate concerns

Event delegation exploits bubbling: attaching one listener to a common ancestor and checking event.target lets you handle events for many, or dynamically added, children without binding a listener to each one
